newsitem.title: INDIA: India plans to recover huge amounts of black money.
newsitem.headline: India plans to recover huge amounts of black money.

text.p: India plans to recover huge amounts of black money that virtually shores up a parallel economy in the country to help ease the government's cash crunch, a senior planning commission official said on Tuesday.

Madhu Dandavate, deputy chairman of the national Planning Commission, told reporters he planned persuasive and punitive measures to unearth an estimated 80 billion rupees ($2.2 billion) to help ease the crunch.
He did not say what specific measures he had in mind.
Indian officials estimate the country's black money variously at between 50 and 60 percent of the national income.
Dandavate was apparently referring to the amounts calculated by the government as lost due to ineffective tax collection and continued smuggling each year, they said.

"Of the total Indian population (of more than 900 million) only the salaried people, who make up 0.8 percent of the population, pay their income tax honestly," Dandavate, a socialist and a former finance minister, said.

Indian officials estimate billions of dollars are lost annually due to dishonest business practices, including over and under invoicing of trade bills. "Digging out the black money and broadening the income tax collection net will help mobilise a huge resource base," Dandavate said.

India's economic woes were initially blamed on its bureacratic "licence raj" regarded as a fertile ground to breed corruption. It was believed that economic reforms launched by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao during his 1991-96 tenure would help weed out corruption.
But Rao led his Congress party to its worst defeat in general elections this year, blamed largely on a string of corruption scandals surrounding his cabinet colleagues.
Dandavate is on a tour of seven northeastern states, among the most economically backward regions in the country.
